mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past six months indicates strong economic growth, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active when GDPC1 is rising.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate over the past six months is negative in more than 50% of the 20-day return periods, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 20-day returns is below 0.1 (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to lower equity valuations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal activates when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% in more than 70% of the 20-day return periods, but the average return is positive (mean > 0), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in labor force participation (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong economic conditions that boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal activates when both PAYEMS and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages.
failure_condition: Both PAYEMS and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages in more than 60% of the periods, but the average 20-day return is negative (mean < 0), or the interaction term in a regression has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve typically implements monetary tightening, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active only in high-inflation regimes.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, the average 20-day return is positive (mean > 0), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. The signal is always active when INDPRO is rising.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth rate over the past two months is negative in more than 50% of the 5-day return periods, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and 5-day returns is below 0.1 (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (RSAFS) above $350 billion indicates strong housing market activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal activates when RSAFS exceeds $350 billion.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 350000 in more than 70% of the 60-day return periods, but the average return is negative (mean < 0), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in employment (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. The signal activates when UNRATE falls below 4.5% and PAYEMS rises above 135000 (thousands of persons).
failure_condition: Both conditions are met in more than 60% of the periods, but the average 5-day return is negative (mean < 0), or the interaction term in a regression has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of monetary policy tightening (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% and CPIAUCSL rising above 2.5% YoY), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is active only in a monetary tightening regime.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening regime, the average 60-day return is positive (mean > 0), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
